atoms.canonical_statement: The report presents two case reports of plateau iris syndrome in young patients whose diagnoses arose during ophthalmologic evaluation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We hereby present two case reports of plateau iris syndrome in young patients who came to an ophthalmologic consult by chance.

atoms.canonical_statement: The article distinguishes plateau iris configuration from plateau iris syndrome, defining syndrome as recurrent gonioscopically confirmed angle closure after patent iridotomy without central anterior-chamber shallowing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the latter refers to a post laser iridotomy condition in which a patent iridotomy has removed the relative pupillary block

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 was a 43-year-old woman with moderate hyperopia who requested evaluation for blurred right-eye vision during her daughter’s follow-up visit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: mother requests a consult for herself as vision became blurry for some time in OD.

population.label: Case 1: 43-year-old woman with moderate hyperopia and blurred right-eye vision

atoms.canonical_statement: In Case 1, right-eye visual-field testing showed marked loss with mean deviation -30.88 dB, pattern standard deviation 6.88 dB, and a central/paracentral scotoma; the left field was reported normal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: OD reduced retinal sensitivity (MD = -30.88 dB) and central/paracentral scotoma (PSD=6.88 dB)

atoms.canonical_statement: In Case 1, the anterior chamber was shallow peripherally but had normal central depth, and intraocular pressure was 70 mmHg OD and 36 mmHg OS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Anterior segment: AO shallow anterior chamber in periphery, but normal depth in the center

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 fundus examination showed almost total right-eye excavation (C/D=1; printed vertical/horizontal values 1/0.9) and a left-eye C/D ratio of 0.5/0.4.
Case 1 indentation gonioscopy showed a steep peripheral iris approach followed by central flattening over the ciliary body, producing the double-hump sign.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: iris drapes over the ciliary body producing the double “hump” aspect on indentation

atoms.canonical_statement: For Case 1, the authors prescribed intravenous 20% mannitol, systemic acetazolamide, and topical pilocarpine 2% after diagnosing plateau iris syndrome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: prescribe manitol 20% ( iv) and acetazolamide plus Pilocarpine 2% topically.

exposures.details: Source reports 20% concentration; no administered dose amount is given.

atoms.canonical_statement: After Case 1 intraocular pressure decreased to a satisfactory level, peripheral laser iridotomy and argon laser peripheral iridoplasty were performed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a peripheral laser iridotomy (IP) was done along with an ALPI procedure

atoms.canonical_statement: After peripheral iridotomy plus argon laser peripheral iridoplasty in Case 1, right-eye intraocular pressure was 21 mmHg.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP after laser procedures was 21 mmHg in OD

quantitative_result.original_result_text: IOP after laser procedures was 21 mmHg in OD

atoms.canonical_statement: After peripheral iridotomy plus argon laser peripheral iridoplasty in Case 1, left-eye intraocular pressure was 15 mmHg without adjuvant medication.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: in OS the IOP was 15 mmHg without any adjuvant medication.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: in OS the IOP was 15 mmHg without any adjuvant medication.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the last reported Case 1 control, intraocular pressure was 15 mmHg in both eyes after prior laser procedures and pilocarpine withdrawal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: last control showed open angle/ 3600 (Schaffer II or III) and IOP in both eyes was 15 mmHg.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: IOP in both eyes was 15 mmHg.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the last reported Case 1 control, the angle was open through 360 degrees (Schaffer II or III), with continued three-monthly IOP and gonioscopy surveillance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patient remained under supervision for IOP and gonioscopy each 3 months; last control showed open angle/ 3600 (Schaffer II or III)

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 was a 29-year-old woman referred for bilateral juvenile decompensated glaucoma with ocular pain and bilateral decreased vision, worse in the right eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: B.E, female, 29 years old was referred to our Ophthalmology Clinic for a diagnosis of OU Juvenile decompensated glaucoma.

population.label: Case 2: 29-year-old woman with bilateral juvenile decompensated glaucoma presentation

atoms.canonical_statement: Before referral in Case 2, intraocular pressure had been 38 mmHg OD and 40 mmHg OS and was 19 mmHg OD and 28 mmHg OS under multidrug topical therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Under this treatment IOP was OD=19 mmHg, OS-28mmHg.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the authors’ Case 2 examination, intraocular pressure was 10 mmHg OD and 19 mmHg OS; central corneal thickness was 469 μm OD and 474 μm OS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP-OD=10 mmHg (PGA+BB+CAI), IOP-OS=19 mmHg (PGA+BB+CAI+Brimonidine)

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had shallow peripheral but normal axial anterior-chamber depth; gonioscopy showed 270 degrees of closure, opening to Schaffer IV through 360 degrees with indentation and a positive double-hump sign.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: by indentation the angle opened Schaffer IV/ 3600, “double hump” sign positive

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 visual fields showed MD -3.69 dB and PSD 5.15 dB OD, and MD -5.65 dB and PSD 6.26 dB OS, with central/paracentral and superior arcuate defects respectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: MD=-3.69 dB, PSD=5.15 db. In OS ... MD=-5.65 dB, PSD=6.26 dB

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had bilateral retinal pigment epithelial irregularity, punctate flecks, and chronic sub-neurosensory macular fluid; autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy was described as presumed and requiring electrophysiologic confirmation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A presumed diagnosis of autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy (ARB) is suspected by the retina specialist.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had initially undergone laser peripheral iridotomies and later underwent bilateral argon laser peripheral iridoplasty because the left angle remained potentially occludable.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: She underwent a bilateral ALPI procedure without complication

exposures.details: Performed before the reported bilateral ALPI; exact timing not reported.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the last reported Case 2 visit, intraocular pressure was 16 mmHg in each eye while receiving a beta blocker plus carbonic anhydrase inhibitor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: IOP-OD=16 mmHg; IOP-OS=16 mmHg (BB+CAI)

atoms.canonical_statement: After bilateral argon laser peripheral iridoplasty in Case 2, repeat gonioscopy showed improved angle depth, and at the last visit the angle was not considered occludable.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: At the last visit, the angle does not appear to be occludable

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that periodic gonioscopy remains important even after a successful iridotomy because the angle may remain incompletely open or narrow further with age.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Even after a successful iridotomy resulting in a well-open angle, periodic gonioscopy remains crucial

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors describe argon laser peripheral iridoplasty as the procedure of choice for an angle that remains occluded after successful laser iridotomy, citing prior literature for durability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Argon laser peripheral iridoplasty (ALPI) is the procedure of choice to effectively open an angle that remains occluded after successful laser iridotomy.
